prompt: Since 09:40 the chat-gateway fleet behind alb-chat-prod is dropping quiet WebSocket clients: telemetry shows 4,100 close events/hour, 96% code 1006, almost all on connections idle 60-70s. Reconnect volume is up 5x and agents lose presence while reading long threads. No deploys since yesterday and server logs show no errors. Find why idle connections die and stop the drops.

At 14:05 the edge team cut traffic over to the new nginx ingress tier at api-edge.example.com. Since then every new WebSocket connect to /realtime fails: browsers log 'Error during WebSocket handshake: Unexpected response code: 200' at ~900 failures/min, while already-established sessions keep streaming. curl against a backend pod directly still returns 101. Restore successful upgrades through the new edge.

ticker-stream pods (8 pods, 4GiB limit each) began OOMKilling every ~3h after this morning's market-data change to 50 msg/s per symbol. Each kill drops ~6k subscribers and triggers a reconnect spike. Grafana shows pod RSS sawtoothing to 4GiB while connection counts stay flat near 6,200 per pod. Identify what is eating memory and make the fleet stable.

Every deploy of notify-hub (120k concurrent clients, 6 pods) causes a 5-minute outage: rolling restart finishes in 40s, then connect success drops to 30%, pod CPU pins at 100%, and the LB spills 503s at 8k/min before things settle. Deploys are now frozen by the on-call lead. Make deploys non-disruptive for connected clients.

collab-docs scales 12 to 6 pods on the nightly scale-in at 02:00. Since last week's HPA change, every scale-in produces ~9k SESSION_NOT_FOUND errors over 10 minutes and users get kicked to a cold document view. Reconnects succeed (WS 101, auth OK) but the server rejects the resume frame. Stop scale-ins from destroying live sessions.

push-edge-4 stops accepting new WebSocket connections every evening near peak: accept() fails with EMFILE, the gateway logs 'too many open files' from 19:20, and the node flatlines at 65,529 connections while its 3 siblings grow past 80k. CPU sits at 40%, memory at 55% — plenty of headroom. Let the node reach its hardware capacity.

After yesterday's rollout enabling permessage-deflate on stream-hub, egress bandwidth dropped 60% as hoped, but node RSS rose from 6GiB to 19GiB at the same 44k connections and the oldest node OOMed at 03:10. Compression must stay for the mobile data budget, but memory per connection has to come down. Investigate and fix it.

sports-live clients intermittently render a final score, then flip back to an earlier score for ~2s. Incidents line up 1:1 with WS reconnects (~14k/day after network blips). Kafka partitions are keyed per match, the gateway is single-writer per connection, and ordering inside a stable connection is provably fine. Find where ordering breaks and guarantee monotonic updates.

ops-console users are kicked to the login screen every hour on the dot; WS sessions die after exactly 60 minutes regardless of activity — the lifetime scatter plot is a vertical line at 3,600s. The client error dashboard attributes 100% of these drops to 'network instability'. Auth team swears refresh tokens work in the REST flow. Diagnose and keep sessions alive past an hour.

The new bulk-annotate feature in imaging-review fails for ~15% of saves: the WS connection dies right after submitting large annotation sets, client logs show close code 1009 'message too big', and the client retry loop re-sends the same payload forever. Small saves are unaffected; failing payloads cluster around 1.8MB. Make large saves succeed without breaking existing clients.

chat-relay reports 92k connected clients but product analytics says at most 60k users are online; the gap widens ~1.5k/day and broadcast CPU grew 40% in three weeks. ss on the relays shows every socket ESTABLISHED. A restart snaps the count back to ~58k, then the creep resumes. Find why dead clients linger and reclaim the capacity.

msg-router gateway pods (8 of them) sit at 85-95% CPU even though only 3,100 messages/s are published fleet-wide; a flame graph puts 78% of cycles in the Redis subscriber callback. The Redis primary burns 70% of one core. Delivery p95 is 900ms, up from 40ms last month. Cut the fanout waste and restore latency.

Since last Tuesday's az-a incident, dash-stream pods in az-b and az-c run at 91% memory with ~21k WebSocket connections each while az-a pods idle near 3k; two az-b pods OOMKilled yesterday. The NLB reports all 9 targets healthy and new connects arrive at only ~40/s fleet-wide. Rebalance the fleet before the next OOM.

field-ops mobile users on carrier networks report notifications arriving 2-4 minutes late whenever the app has been idle; on office Wi-Fi the same builds deliver in under a second. mobile-push-gw sends server pings every 50s and its dashboards look clean. About 34% of mobile sessions show delivery gaps. Make idle mobile sessions receive pushes within 5 seconds.
